headline: TOUR WEEK ARRIVES: CORN, WHEAT LED FRIDAY HIGHER
subheadline: Pro Farmer scouts hit the road Monday; Friday's close sets the stakes for what they find.
lead: Corn closed Friday at $4.59, up 9 cents, and wheat finished at $6.74, up 17 cents. Both moves came on fund and technical buying into a week that will either validate or punish those positions. The Pro Farmer Crop Tour starts Monday with USDA already on record at 180.7 bushels per acre on corn. Whatever the scouts find, it hits a market that went into the weekend leaning bullish.
the_takeaway: Tour week reprices the crop or confirms USDA; either way, this market moves by Friday.
teaser: Corn ran 9 cents Friday. Now the scouts go find out if the crop earned it.

one_number.context: USDA's Aug 12 survey-based yield came in 2.3 bushels below July's 183.0. Pro Farmer's national number, due Friday Aug 21, is the first independent cross-check. Our own nowcast sat at 183.6 before the WASDE. We were wrong. The tour is the next data point.

sections.title: GRAINS ENTER TOUR WEEK LEANING BULLISH
sections.body:
- Corn closed at **$4.59** nearby and **$4.84** December on Friday, both up roughly 2%, with fund and technical buying the stated driver into a week that prices the actual crop.
- Wheat at **$6.74** added 17 cents, near the top of its 52-week range, on deteriorating Russian output under sanctions and refinery attacks.
- USDA is already at 180.7 bu/acre on corn; if Pro Farmer scouts return above 182, Friday's gains get sold hard by Wednesday.
sections.bottom_line: Bullish positioning is in the market before a single scout sample exists. That is the risk.
sections.farmer_action: Old-crop corn sellers: $4.59 held into the weekend. Wednesday's tour summary is your exit trigger; above 182 bu/acre from scouts, the board softens. Do not wait for Friday.

sections.title: BEANS LAG, BUT TOUR WEEK IS THE REAL TEST
sections.body:
- Soybeans closed at **$11.76** nearby and $11.91 November, up less than half a percent Friday, still trailing corn and wheat on a relative basis all week.
- Pod-fill is the Aug. crop story now; favorable weather in the central Belt is keeping a ceiling on bean upside even as China's $17 billion annual US ag purchase commitment (May 18 deal, through 2028) provides a demand floor.
- USDA pegged soybean yield at 52.7 bu/acre Aug. 12; record production of 4.519 billion bushels is in the cards if that holds, and carryout rising to 320 million keeps the carry structure wide.
sections.catalyst: USDA Aug WASDE soy yield 52.7 bu/acre, record-pace production; China purchase commitment supporting demand floor.
sections.bottom_line: Beans are not the tour story corn is; a scout number above 53 bushels per acre adds pressure to an already comfortable balance sheet.

sections.title: CATTLE SLIP ON FUND EXIT, STRUCTURAL STORY INTACT
sections.body:
- Live cattle closed at **$223.75**, down 1.1% Friday, with fund liquidation the stated driver as the week's direct cash business stayed unsettled late.
- Feeders at $341.27, off half a percent, are holding historic territory even as the market starts pricing the Aug. 24 phased reopening at Douglas, AZ of Mexican feeder imports, the screwworm-driven closure of Mexican feeder cattle imports that tightened supply all summer.
- The structural read: high costs and supply constraints will keep beef prices elevated, but the fund money is stepping back until the cash trade clarifies and the import picture firms.
sections.catalyst: Fund liquidation Friday; Mexican feeder import reopening Aug 24 at Douglas AZ beginning to weigh on feeder premium.
sections.bottom_line: Cattle's structural bid is real, but Aug 24 is the near-term pivot; feeder/live spread is the tell.
sections.vs_yesterday: Cattle: fund exit accelerated Friday vs Thursday's drift.

sections.title: CRUDE FIRMS, FERTILIZER PRESSURE LINGERS
sections.body:
- WTI closed at **$82.40**, up 1.3% Friday, with Somali piracy increasing as the effective Hormuz closure forces commercial shipping onto longer African routes, adding a freight premium that is separate from the crude supply story.
- Fertilizer prices are projected to stay elevated through 2028 per Feedstuffs, with geopolitical supply chain disruptions the stated driver; $5-plus diesel is already squeezing fall fieldwork margins by an estimated $1.4 billion nationally.
- Natural gas at $2.71, near the bottom of its 52-week range, is not the input cost problem this fall; diesel is.
sections.catalyst: Somali piracy rising on Hormuz rerouting; fertilizer elevated-through-2028 forecast; $5-plus diesel $1.4B farm margin squeeze reported.
sections.bottom_line: Diesel is the input story for fall harvest, not crude headlines; lock what you can before fieldwork starts.

outside_the_pit.title: Rail merger rejection sought by grain shippers on service concerns
outside_the_pit.body: The Soy Transportation Coalition and other grain groups are calling on regulators to reject the Union Pacific-Norfolk Southern merger application, citing failure to meet minimum service standards. A merged rail giant controlling more corridor capacity raises freight cost and scheduling risk for producers who depend on rail to the Gulf.

outside_the_pit.title: Fertilizer prices seen staying elevated through 2028, geopolitics the driver
outside_the_pit.body: Feedstuffs reports geopolitical conflicts and supply chain disruptions will keep fertilizer prices and availability under pressure well past this crop year. Producers pricing 2027 and 2028 inputs should treat elevated costs as a planning baseline, not a temporary move higher to wait out.

the_more_you_know.title: The number scouts look for that price doesn't: ear flex.
the_more_you_know.body: Pro Farmer scouts measure ear girth and kernel row counts in the field, not satellite imagery. A high kernel-row count with short ear flex says the plant ran out of room and yield is capped. USDA's 180.7 already reflects a stress signal. Scouts confirming short-flex ears in two or more key states by Wednesday would validate that number fast.

watch_list.desc: Pro Farmer Crop Tour opens; Indiana and Ohio are first-day states. Watch for ear sample reports by evening; below 170 bu/acre field averages in Indiana adds corn premium Tuesday.
USDA Crop Progress; corn condition rated good/excellent below 60% raises yield-cut odds; above 65% puts pressure on the bull position built Friday.
Weekly Export Sales; beans under 300K MT keeps the carry structure in charge and questions the China demand floor narrative.
Pro Farmer national yield estimates released; corn above 182 bu/acre is a sell trigger; below 180 accelerates December corn toward $4.95.
